articles.title: Claude Code Remote Control stops when you close the lid. Here's why, and the fix

Turn on Push when actions required in /config and permission prompts and questions arrive as pushes. Then you close the MacBook lid, and the session goes quiet. Why The session runs on your Mac. Remote Control is a window into it, not a copy of it. When the Mac sleeps, Claude stops. The docs say exactly this: if your laptop sleeps or your network drops, Claude Code reconnects automatically when your machine comes back online. So it reconnects afterwards. Nothing runs while the Mac is asleep, and the message you sent from your phone waits until the lid opens again. Closing the lid without an external display puts a MacBook to sleep regardless of caffeinate. Claude Code already runs caffeinate -i while it works, which only blocks idle sleep. What Is Apache Iggy and Why It Exists Can you tell us a bit about Apache Iggy? Apache Iggy is a persistent message streaming platform written in Rust. It stores messages in streams, topics, and partitions as an append-only log, while consumers read independently or through consumer groups. The server is distributed as a single binary with no external broker or database dependency. It supports TCP, QUIC, WebSocket, and HTTP, and provides SDKs for Rust, C#, C++, Java, Go, Python, Node.js, and PHP. You write a service.json, you run flisk up (the GitHub README still says tdk up for the same package), and it generates the local Docker and Tilt wiring so those services start on your machine. Production stays on Helm. That is the whole product sentence, and it is a small sentence on purpose. The interesting question is not whether the binary is big. articles.title: Azure Workload Identity: Remove Secrets From Your AKS Pods in 45 Minutes
articles.summary: If you are still mounting a Kubernetes Secret containing an AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET into your pods, you are one kubectl get secret -o yaml away from an incident report. And if you are using AAD Pod Identity, you are running a component that reached end of support in September 2023. Azure Workload Identity replaces both. It uses the OIDC issuer built into your AKS cluster to let a Kubernetes ServiceAccount exchange its projected token for an Azure AD (Microsoft Entra ID) access token. No secret, no rotation job, no NodeManagedIdentity DaemonSet intercepting IMDS traffic. This walkthrough takes about 45 minutes end to end, assuming you already have an AKS cluster and the Azure CLI installed. articles.title: I built Kule: AI agents work on a copy of your folder, and you decide what comes back
articles.summary: Hi, I'm Selçuk. I've been building an open-source tool called Kule, and its first preview release is out. I'd like to tell you what it does, why I built it, and what it can't do yet. The short version: Kule is a control room for AI agents that work on your folders. You point an agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or any agent that speaks ACP) at a folder. Kule gives it a copy-on-write copy of that folder inside a sandbox, looks at what every command really changed, and lets nothing reach the real folder until a policy, or you, says so. Every commit can be undone. ("Kule" means tower in Turkish. Think control tower.) The problem I kept running into Coding agents are good now, good enough that we let them run commands. When an agent runs a command, it runs as you: your files, your ~/.ssh and ~/.aws, your ~/.zshrc, your network, your API keys. articles.title: We gave our MCP server an undo button
articles.summary: Letting an AI agent change your product's settings is only reasonable if you can take it all back. So every change our MCP server makes goes into a run that can be undone in one step. This is how it works, and the decisions that turned out to be hard. In July 2025, Replit's AI agent deleted a company's production database during a code freeze, then told the user the data couldn't be recovered. It could. Replit had a rollback, and the user restored everything from a checkpoint. The agent just didn't know the feature existed. Two lessons from that story shaped what we built: the agent has to know that undo exists, and people have to be able to undo without asking the agent. We build Privatrak, a cookieless analytics tool. Its MCP server lets Claude, Cursor or Codex do more than read your analytics.
